tool_summary: Fedora and newer RHEL's package manager, the successor to yum. Same install/remove/scriptlet risk shape as yum, with a largely compatible command surface.
platform_notes: dnf is specific to Fedora and newer RHEL/CentOS Stream releases.

rules.description: The --nogpgcheck flag disables GPG signature verification for the packages being installed, removing the primary protection against tampered packages.
rules.reversible_note: The package can be removed, but its install-time scriptlets may have already made changes beyond the package's own files.

rules.description: The config-manager --add-repo subcommand adds a third-party repository as a trusted package source. Unlike yum-config-manager (a separate binary on older systems), config-manager is a built-in dnf subcommand on modern systems, so this rule can match it directly. An untrusted or unfamiliar repository is a common supply-chain attack vector.
Installs a package, running arbitrary %post scriptlets with root privileges at install time.
rules.reversible_note: The package can be removed, but install-time scriptlets may have already made changes beyond the package's own files.

rules.description: Manages system packages. Read-only subcommands (list, info, search) do not alter system state.
